answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with identity-bound stake. Each agent registers one keypair and locks collateral under it; a vote counts only while that lock is bonded. To fabricate a thousand voters an attacker must post a thousand separate locks, so cost grows linearly, and a double vote slashes the stake. Even a raider holding an onyx treasury cannot mint cheap voices by pushing funds across a bridge into the nebula registry, because each new key pays its own deposit and detection burns it.
